summary: 3 findings checked: 2 confirmed (RG-001 by the saved verify-run plus a version-gate site-check, TP-R2-001 by site-check), 1 unverifiable (HW2-001: the unlocked read-modify-write and its cross-process writers exist, but no concurrent run reproduced a lost update).

verifications.evidence: P/research-evidence/verify-RG-001-1.txt (exit 0): `git show b147408a8:src/integrations/issues-board.ts | sed -n 94,106p` prints listUrl with `!["assigned", "created", "mentioned", "subscribed"].includes(source) || ... throw new Error(invalidInput)`, so a base-era keryx rejects source "repository"; `git grep -n DEFAULT_SOURCE 88e3faba9 -- apps/desktop/src/issues` shows model.ts:15 `export const DEFAULT_SOURCE: IssueSource = "repository"` and IssuesBoard.tsx:64 falling back to it when no source is stored. The check would have shown "repository" in the base allow-list if the finding were false; it did not. Supplementary site-check: `git diff --stat b147408a8..88e3faba9 -- apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/version.rs package.json apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/issues.rs apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/locator.rs` is empty; MIN_KERYX_VERSION stays "0.4.50" (version.rs:9) and package.json is 0.4.53 at both base and head, so a published keryx 0.4.50-0.4.53 that predates the PR still passes the Automatic-mode version gate and is used. `keryx ctx rg` over apps/desktop/src/platform/issues.ts finds the bundled-CLI hint only for "does not support Issues" (line 13) and "Incompatible Issues response" (line 18), and useIssueCollection.ts:17 isAccessError matches only access|account_mismatch|source_unavailable. Not run: Desktop end-to-end against an older keryx binary.

P/research-evidence/verify-TP-R2-001-1.txt (exit 0): `git grep -n 'setTimeout(resolve, 40)' 88e3faba9 -- apps/desktop/src/test` returns exactly the two named sites, app-navigation.fixture.tsx:287 and app-work-row.fixture.tsx:88, each `const settle = () => React.act(async () => { await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 40)); });`. `keryx ctx rg --all -c 'settle\(\)'` counts 5 uses in app-work-row.fixture.tsx and 11 in app-navigation.fixture.tsx. Both are new in this PR: `git grep -n 'setTimeout(resolve, 40)' b147408a8 -- apps/desktop/src/test` exits 1, `git grep -c 'settle()' b147408a8 -- apps/desktop/src/test/app-navigation.fixture.tsx` finds none, app-work-row.fixture.tsx is absent at base (`git cat-file -e` fatal), and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 21030edf0 b147408a8` exits 1. The claim is a code-shape claim (fixed delay used as the async sync point) and the check settles it. Not reproduced: an actual CI flake.

P/research-evidence/verify-HW2-001-1.txt (exit 0) plus follow-up git grep at 88e3faba9: organize.ts:117-138 updateSessionFlagsAt = readSessionFlags(dir) -> `{ ...current }` merge -> writeFlags(dir, next) (line 136), writeFlags = writeOwnerOnlyFileAtomic (line 109); `git grep -n -i -e lock -e withFile 88e3faba9 -- src/session/organize.ts` exits 1 (no lock); setSessionFlags (152-161) delegates straight to it; server.ts:2964 calls setSessionFlags with no lock around it; issue-session.ts:53 bindIssueSubject and issues-launch.ts:116 are the other two non-test writers. All four named sites exist and the read-modify-write is unlocked, so the shape is real. The claimed consequence (a lost update when two keryx processes write one session's flags.json at once) was not reproduced: no concurrent two-process run was executed, and the process model (one ACP server per window, issue-workspace as a separate child) was not checked here. The site check cannot separate the claimed race from a write order that never overlaps in practice.
